μP + Muon is the default, so training at any preset just works — `train.lr` is the
μP base LR (`0.01`), reused unchanged at every size:

```bash
oplm train --preset 1B data.train=/data/uniref50/   # μP + Muon + lr 0.01, by default
```

The defaults live in `configs/train/base.yaml` (`optimizer: muon`,
`muon_adjust_lr_fn: original`, `lr: 0.01`) and `configs/model/base.yaml`
(`mup_enable: true`, `mup_base_width: 512`). With μP on, **`train.lr` is the base
LR** and transfers across width — you do not re-tune it per preset.

**To re-tune the base LR** for a new optimizer or data regime, follow the phased
production workflow in [LR_SWEEP.md](LR_SWEEP.md). It ranks held-out validation
loss, repeats finalists across three seeds, verifies transfer across the preset
ray, and measures the production-batch correction.

**To disable μP** (vanilla ESM-C recipe — AdamW plus the pre-2026 architecture,
e.g. for an ablation), apply the opt-out overlay — note its `lr` is a plain AdamW
LR that must be tuned per size:
===

### μP (maximal update parametrization)

μP makes a learning rate tuned on a small proxy model transfer to much larger
models without re-sweeping at every scale. It is **on by default** for `oplm train`
runs (with `train.optimizer=muon`, `train.muon_adjust_lr_fn=original`,
`train.lr=0.01`), and a no-op at the base width. See [MUP.md](MUP.md) for the full
recipe and the tune-once-reuse-`train.lr` workflow; disable it with
`configs/train/vanilla_esm-c.yaml`.

> **Run defaults vs. dataclass fallbacks.** The `Default` column below (and in the
> Train table) is the **run default** from `configs/*/base.yaml` — what `oplm train`
> loads. Bare Python construction (`OplmConfig()` / `TrainConfig()`) and
> `from_pretrained` use conservative fallbacks instead (`mup_enable=false`,
> `optimizer=adamw`, `lr=1e-4`, `norm_strategy=pre`, `attn_output_gate=none`,
> `value_residual=none`, `canon_enabled=false`), so direct use and existing
> checkpoints are unaffected.

| Override | Type | Default | Valid values / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model.mup_enable` | `bool` | `true` | Master switch (run default; dataclass fallback `false`). When `false`, init, forward multipliers, and per-group LRs are identical to non-μP runs. |
| `model.mup_base_width` | `int` | `512` | `hidden_size` of the proxy/base model where `m = hidden_size / mup_base_width` equals 1. The production sweep overrides this fallback/default with its forced 768-wide anchor. Must be `≥ 1`. |
| `model.mup_output_mult` | `float` | `1.0` | Tunable O(1) multiplier on the output logits (applied as `mup_output_mult / m` on the readout matmul path). Must be `> 0`. |

**`batch_mult` is ranking metadata only — it is never re-applied to a config.** `bridge` records
each candidate's batch-correction multiplier as `batch_mult` and folds the correction directly
into that candidate's `lr` (`lr = candidate["lr"] * multiplier`); every later phase (`confirm`,
`scale`) carries `batch_mult` forward purely so you can see which batch correction a winner came
from, but reads only `lr`, `output_mult`, and `depth_exponent` back out of a selected candidate.
There is no `train.batch_mult` training-config field, and there must not be one applied by hand
either — the correction is already inside `lr`. Re-applying `batch_mult` on top of that `lr` would
square the correction.

## Production WSD schedule

The sweep and 100k scaling cells select the peak stable learning rate; they do not select the
production cooldown. Production uses:

```text
linear warmup
-> 1–2M stable-LR steps
-> 0.5–1M linear-decay steps
```

Configure `scheduler=wsd_linear`, set `stable_steps` to the plateau length, and set `max_steps`
to warmup plus plateau plus decay. For example:

```yaml
train:
  scheduler: wsd_linear
  lr: 0.01  # illustrative; replace with the confirmed production LR
  min_lr: 0.0
  warmup_steps: 10_000
  stable_steps: 1_500_000
  max_steps: 2_260_000  # 10k warmup + 1.5M stable + 750k decay
```

**Watch out for a zero-decay footgun.** The sweep phases in this document deliberately set
`stable_steps = max_steps - warmup_steps` for every proxy cell — for a *short* proxy run that
convention is fine, since selection only cares about the peak stable LR, not a cooldown. That same
arithmetic is **wrong** for a real production run: it leaves **zero** steps between the end of the
stable plateau and `max_steps`, so a `wsd_linear` schedule trains at peak LR all the way to the
end with no decay at all — silently, since nothing errors. This is not a hypothetical: this
repo's own production job scripts previously shipped with exactly that configuration.
`configs/scaling.yaml` gets this right — `warmup_steps: 5000`, `stable_steps: 85000`,
`max_steps: 100000`, leaving a real 10,000-step (10%) linear-decay tail — and is the reference to
copy the pattern from, not the short-horizon sweep cells.

Preserve optimizer state through the small dataset-mixture change at the stable-to-decay
transition. Do not reset momentum or add a second warmup.

# μP: Learning-Rate Transfer Across Width

**Maximal Update Parameterization (μP)** lets a learning rate tuned on a small
proxy model transfer to much larger models without re-sweeping at every scale.
Tune `train.lr` **once** at a small proxy width, then reuse the same number at
every larger preset.

μP + Muon is the **default training recipe** (`oplm train` uses it out of the box;
`train.lr` defaults to the μP base LR `0.01`). It is a **no-op at the base width** —
at `hidden_size == mup_base_width`, init, forward multipliers, and per-group LRs
are bit-identical to a non-μP run. The production optimizer for μP is **Muon**;
AdamW is also supported. To turn μP off (and recover the conventional ESM-C
recipe — AdamW plus the pre-2026 architecture), apply
`configs/train/vanilla_esm-c.yaml` (see §1).

Backward-compatibility note: the default lives in the **YAML run-config layer**
(`configs/*/base.yaml`). Bare `OplmConfig()` / `TrainConfig()` construction and
`from_pretrained` stay μP-off (the conservative dataclass fallback), and existing
checkpoints load with whatever `mup_enable` they were saved with.

Related references:

- [TRAIN.md](TRAIN.md) — the general training how-to.
- [CONFIG.md](CONFIG.md#μp-maximal-update-parametrization) — the μP model and training knobs.
- [MODEL_ARCHITECTURE.md](MODEL_ARCHITECTURE.md) — the model itself.

- **Muon's `original` factor** multiplies per-param LR by `√(max(1, d_out/d_in))`
  — a function of *aspect ratio only*. Aspect ratio is approximately constant
  across presets, so the Muon **base LR is constant across width** (the residual
  error from FFN rounding is validated empirically by the coord-check).

### Owner-by-optimizer

- **Muon mode** (`optimizer=muon`): `q/k/v/o, gate/up/down` → Muon at a constant
  `lr`. Only `lm_head.dense` stays on AdamW and takes `lr/m`; `lm_head.decoder`
  (the readout) also stays on AdamW, at `lr ×1`.
- **AdamW-only mode** (`optimizer=adamw`): hidden matrices take `lr/m_W` (`lr/m`
  for hidden-fan-in matrices, `lr/m_ffn` for `down_proj`); embedding, the readout
  `lm_head.decoder`, norms, and biases stay at `lr` (×1).

### Optional repeated-block depth correction

Width-μP supplies `width_aware_lr`. When model depth also changes, the optional
empirical correction for parameters inside repeated Transformer blocks is:

```text
effective_block_lr(L) = width_aware_lr * (mup_depth_reference_layers / L) ** mup_depth_lr_exponent
```

`mup_depth_reference_layers` defaults to `24`, and
`mup_depth_lr_exponent=0.0` makes the correction a no-op. The correction does
not apply to embeddings, the final stack norm, or the MLM head/readout.

The exponent is a consequence of the residual parameterization, not a free
hyperparameter: with the branch scaling frozen at `1/√L`
(`residual_scaling=sqrt_num_layers`), summing per-block updates of size
`η·(24/L)^e` over `L` blocks gives a total one-step feature update
`∝ η·L^(1/2−e)`, so depth invariance pins `e = 0.5`. (CompleteP's depth-flat
Adam LR belongs to its `1/L` branch multiplier, `α = 1` — a different design;
its exponent does not graft onto a `1/√L` branch.) The production sweep pins
`0.5` and *verifies* it on a fixed-width depth ray rather than sweeping a grid —
sandwich norm post-normalizes each branch before the `1/√L` multiplier and the
learned gate, and Muon is neither Adam nor SGD, so the derivation is checked
empirically; see [LR_SWEEP.md](LR_SWEEP.md#depth-ray-lr-transfer-check).

content.text:
It's in addition to — and in fact derived *from* — the residual scaling. The two act on different quantities: `residual_scaling=sqrt_num_layers` controls the **forward pass**, while `mup_depth_lr_exponent` controls the **size of optimizer updates**. Neither can do the other's job, and the exponent's value of 0.5 only makes sense *because* the residual scaling is 1/√L.

The intuition, following the derivation in `docs/MUP.md` ("Optional repeated-block depth correction"):

- **Forward:** each block's branch output is multiplied by α = 1/√L before being added to the residual stream. At init the L branch outputs are roughly uncorrelated, so their sum grows like √L, and the 1/√L multiplier cancels it — activations stay O(1) at any depth. That's all residual scaling does.

- **Updates:** take one optimizer step at LR η. All L blocks change at once, and their contributions to the output are *correlated* (they all move in the loss-decreasing direction), so they add roughly linearly, not like √L. The total one-step feature change is ≈ L blocks × η per block × the 1/√L branch multiplier ∝ η·√L. So even with perfect forward-pass depth stability, a *deeper* model takes effectively *larger* steps at the same base LR — which is exactly why the tuned LR wouldn't transfer from the 24-layer proxy to deeper presets.

The depth correction fixes that second problem: each repeated block gets LR η·(24/L)^e, making the total update ∝ η·L^(1/2−e). Depth invariance pins **e = 0.5** — the exponent is a consequence of the 1/√L branch scaling, not an independent knob. (Under a different residual design, e.g. CompleteP's α = 1/L, the required exponent would be different; the two settings come as a matched pair.) Because sandwich norm and Muon complicate the clean theory, the sweep didn't trust the derivation blindly — it pinned 0.5 and *verified* it empirically on the fixed-width depth ray (`docs/LR_SWEEP.md`, depth-ray transfer check), which is what the `a0.5` in your confirm cells reflects.

Two practical notes: the correction is exactly 1.0 at the 24-layer reference depth (the 170M anchor), so it changes nothing on the proxy where the LR was tuned — it only kicks in as `num_hidden_layers` departs from 24 (e.g. the default 32-layer model gets hidden-block LR × (24/32)^0.5 ≈ 0.87). And it applies only to parameters inside repeated blocks — embeddings, the final stack norm, and the MLM head/readout are untouched.

The timer is opt-in; in this repo only `configs/scaling.yaml` enables it (`save_every_minutes: 30`).
- To turn it off where a config has enabled it: `save_every_minutes: null` in YAML, or `train.save_every_minutes=null` as a CLI dotlist override (the config loader parses `null` to `None`).

205	            raise ValueError(f"muon_momentum must be >= 0, got {self.muon_momentum}")

210	        if self.gradient_accumulation_steps < 1:

213	            )

215	            raise ValueError(
216	                f"throughput_warmup_steps must be >= 0, got {self.throughput_warmup_steps}"
217	            )
218	        if self.peak_tflops is not None and self.peak_tflops <= 0:
219	            raise ValueError(f"peak_tflops must be > 0, got {self.peak_tflops}")
220	        if not math.isfinite(self.mup_depth_lr_exponent) or self.mup_depth_lr_exponent < 0:
221	            raise ValueError(
222	                f"mup_depth_lr_exponent must be finite and >= 0, got {self.mup_depth_lr_exponent}"
223	            )
224	        if self.mup_depth_reference_layers < 1:
225	            raise ValueError(
226	                f"mup_depth_reference_layers must be >= 1, got {self.mup_depth_reference_layers}"
227	            )
228	        if self.stability_probe_every < 0:
229	            raise ValueError(
230	                f"stability_probe_every must be >= 0, got {self.stability_probe_every}"
231	            )
232	        if self.save_every_minutes is not None and self.save_every_minutes <= 0:
233	            raise ValueError(
234	                f"save_every_minutes must be > 0 when set, got {self.save_every_minutes}"
235	            )
236	        if self.keep_every_n_steps is not None and self.keep_every_n_steps <= 0:
237	            raise ValueError(
238	                f"keep_every_n_steps must be > 0 when set, got {self.keep_every_n_steps}"
239	            )
240	        if self.keep_every_n_hours is not None and self.keep_every_n_hours <= 0:
241	            raise ValueError(
242	                f"keep_every_n_hours must be > 0 when set, got {self.keep_every_n_hours}"
243	            )
244	        if self.dist_timeout_minutes <= 0:
245	            raise ValueError(f"dist_timeout_minutes must be > 0, got {self.dist_timeout_minutes}")

247	            raise ValueError(
248	                f"parallelism must be one of {_VALID_PARALLELISM}, got {self.parallelism!r}"

252	            # unscale_/inf-check runs per rank over local shards without a cross-rank

261	            )

264	            # only, on the documented assumption that "the extra forward has no

266	            # all-gathers sharded parameters. Running it on rank 0 alone would hang every
267	            # other rank until dist_timeout_minutes, then crash-loop through the requeue.

269	            # stability_probe_every=0).

271	                "parallelism='hsdp' is incompatible with stability_diagnostics=true and "
272	                "stability_probe_every > 0: the diagnostic probe runs a main-process-only "
273	                "forward, which under FSDP2 issues an all-gather that would hang every "
274	                "other rank. Set train.stability_probe_every=0 to keep the (collective-free) "

296	class ScheduleSpec:
297	    """Parsed, behavior-free eval cadence built from an ``every: {unit: N}`` block.
298	
299	    Carries no behavior so it can live in ``oplm.config`` without importing
300	    ``oplm.eval``. The eval harness turns it into a concrete ``Schedule`` via
301	    ``oplm.eval.schedule.build_schedule``.
302	    """

304	    unit: str  # one of _VALID_SCHEDULE_UNITS
305	    n: int  # positive
306	    at_start: bool = False
307	    at_end: bool = True
308	
309	
310	def parse_schedule_block(raw: Any, label: str) -> ScheduleSpec:
311	    """Parse an ``every: {unit: N, at_start?, at_end?}`` mapping into a ScheduleSpec.
312	
313	    Args:
314	        raw: The cadence mapping (a dataset's ``every`` or ``train.eval_every``).
315	        label: Human-readable source used in error messages.
316	
317	    Raises:
318	        ValueError: If ``raw`` is not a mapping, names ``epochs`` (deferred), does not
319	            name exactly one valid unit, has unknown keys, the unit value is not a
320	            positive int, or ``at_start`` / ``at_end`` are not actual bools.
321	    """
322	    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
323	        raise ValueError(
324	            f"{label}: cadence must be a mapping like {{steps: N}} or {{tokens: N}}, "
325	            f"got {type(raw).__name__}"
326	        )
327	    if "epochs" in raw:
328	        raise ValueError(
329	            f"{label}: epoch cadence is not yet supported (see docs/EVAL_HARNESS.md "
330	            f"§4.6); use {{steps: N}} or {{tokens: N}}"
331	        )
332	    unknown = [k for k in raw if k not in _SCHEDULE_KEYS]
333	    if unknown:
334	        raise ValueError(f"{label}: unknown keys in cadence block: {sorted(unknown)}")
335	    unit_keys = [k for k in raw if k in _VALID_SCHEDULE_UNITS]
336	    if len(unit_keys) != 1:
337	        raise ValueError(
338	            f"{label}: cadence must name exactly one of {list(_VALID_SCHEDULE_UNITS)}, "
339	            f"got {sorted(unit_keys)}"
340	        )
341	    unit = unit_keys[0]
342	    n = raw[unit]
343	    if isinstance(n, bool) or not isinstance(n, int) or n <= 0:
344	        raise ValueError(f"{label}: cadence {unit!r} must be a positive int, got {n!r}")
345	    # The schema says bools; parse them strictly. bool(raw.get(...)) would coerce the
346	    # YAML string "false" to True, silently inverting the flag — validate the type.
347	    at_start = raw.get("at_start", False)
348	    at_end = raw.get("at_end", True)
349	    for flag_name, flag_value in (("at_start", at_start), ("at_end", at_end)):
350	        if not isinstance(flag_value, bool):
351	            raise ValueError(
352	                f"{label}: {flag_name!r} must be a bool, got {flag_value!r} "
353	                f"({type(flag_value).__name__})"
354	            )
355	    return ScheduleSpec(unit=unit, n=n, at_start=at_start, at_end=at_end)

391	
392	    # Collation padding: None = pad to batch-longest sequence; N = pad to the
393	    # smallest multiple of N that is >= batch-longest. Useful for compile+static
394	    # regimes (dynamic=False) to reduce unique shapes and improve throughput.

410	            # a bare int check would silently accept True/False.
411	            if isinstance(self.pad_to_multiple_of, bool):
412	                raise ValueError(
413	                    f"pad_to_multiple_of must be an int, got bool ({self.pad_to_multiple_of!r})"
414	                )
415	            if not isinstance(self.pad_to_multiple_of, int):
416	                got = type(self.pad_to_multiple_of).__name__
417	                raise ValueError(f"pad_to_multiple_of must be an int, got {got}")
418	            if self.pad_to_multiple_of < 1:
419	                raise ValueError(f"pad_to_multiple_of must be >= 1, got {self.pad_to_multiple_of}")

423	            raise ValueError(f"random_token_prob must be in [0, 1], got {self.random_token_prob}")
424	        # The remainder (1 - mask_token_prob - random_token_prob) keeps the
425	        # original token, so the two probabilities must not exceed 1 together.
426	        if self.mask_token_prob + self.random_token_prob > 1.0 + 1e-9:
427	            raise ValueError(
428	                "mask_token_prob + random_token_prob must be <= 1, got "
429	                f"{self.mask_token_prob} + {self.random_token_prob} = "
430	                f"{self.mask_token_prob + self.random_token_prob}"

446	def validate_parallelism_compat(cfg: OplmConfig) -> None:
447	    """Reject cross-section config combinations that would deadlock under HSDP.
448	
449	    ``TrainConfig.__post_init__`` validates everything inside ``train.*``; this covers the
450	    one incompatibility that spans sections, so it needs both ``cfg.train`` and
451	    ``cfg.data``. Called from :func:`load_config` (so a CLI/YAML mistake fails at parse
452	    time) and again at the top of ``Trainer.__init__`` (so a directly-constructed config --
453	    tests, sweeps, notebooks -- cannot bypass it). Idempotent and pure; no collectives, and
454	    its inputs are rank-identical, so every rank raises identically.
455	
456	    **Eval under HSDP deadlocks.** ``fully_shard`` mutates the module in place, so
457	    ``accelerator.unwrap_model`` hands the evaluator the ``FSDPModule`` itself, and every
458	    eval forward all-gathers sharded parameters. The eval tasks stripe their work across
459	    ranks (``[rank::world_size]``), so ranks run *different numbers* of forwards -- the
460	    ranks that finish early never issue the matching all-gathers and the group wedges until
461	    ``dist_timeout_minutes``, then crash-loops through the requeue. Making eval
462	    HSDP-safe (rank-padded forward counts, or gathering the model once into an unsharded
463	    eval copy) is follow-up work; until then this refuses the combination up front rather
464	    than letting a multi-node run hang at its first eval.
465	
466	    Args:
467	        cfg: The fully resolved root config.
468	
469	    Raises:
470	        ValueError: ``train.parallelism="hsdp"`` with any eval dataset configured.
471	    """
472	    if cfg.train.parallelism == "hsdp" and cfg.data.eval is not None:
473	        raise ValueError(
474	            "train.parallelism='hsdp' is incompatible with configured eval datasets "
475	            "(data.eval): eval tasks stripe their forwards across ranks, but under FSDP2 "
476	            "every forward all-gathers sharded parameters -- ranks with fewer forwards "
477	            "stop issuing all-gathers and the whole group hangs until dist_timeout_minutes. "
478	            "Run eval as a separate ddp job against the checkpoint, or set "
479	            "train.parallelism='ddp'. See oplm.training.parallel for the limitation and "
480	            "the planned fix."
481	        )

547	def _reject_unknown_model_keys(model_dict: dict[str, Any], model_config_cls: type) -> None:
548	    """Raise on `model.*` keys that no `OplmConfig` field or HF metadata accepts.
549	
550	    `PretrainedConfig.__init__` silently absorbs unknown `**kwargs`, so a typo
551	    like `model.cannon_enabled=true` would otherwise be retained while the real
552	    `canon_enabled` stays at its default — silently disabling an ablation. The
553	    allowed set is the constructor signature plus the HF metadata keys a default
554	    instance emits via `to_dict()` (so serialized configs still round-trip).
555	
556	    Args:
557	        model_dict: The merged `model` subtree about to construct the HF config.
558	        model_config_cls: The `OplmConfig` (HF `PretrainedConfig`) class.
559	
560	    Raises:
561	        ValueError: If `model_dict` contains any key outside the allowed set.
562	    """
563	    params = inspect.signature(model_config_cls.__init__).parameters
564	    allowed = {
565	        name
566	        for name, p in params.items()
567	        if name != "self" and p.kind not in (p.VAR_KEYWORD, p.VAR_POSITIONAL)
568	    }
569	    # HF metadata keys (model_type, transformers_version, architectures, dtype,
570	    # id2label, ...) are not constructor params but round-trip through a
571	    # serialized config; a default instance enumerates exactly that set.
572	    allowed |= set(model_config_cls().to_dict())
573	
574	    unknown = sorted(set(model_dict) - allowed)
575	    if unknown:
576	        raise ValueError(
577	            f"Unknown model config key(s): {unknown}. Check for typos "
578	            "(e.g. 'canon_enabled', not 'cannon_enabled'); valid keys come from "
579	            "OplmConfig.__init__ and HuggingFace PretrainedConfig metadata."
580	        )

583	def load_config(argv: list[str]) -> OplmConfig:
584	    """Load config from defaults, optional preset, optional YAML file, and CLI overrides.
585	
586	    Merge order (later overrides earlier): defaults → preset → YAML file → CLI overrides.
587	
588	    Args:
589	        argv: Command-line arguments (e.g. sys.argv[1:]).
590	            Supports ``--preset <name>`` for size presets, ``--config <path>``
591	            for YAML files, ``--name <run>`` for the W&B run name, and dotlist
592	            overrides like ``model.num_hidden_layers=32``.
593	
594	    Returns:
595	        Fully resolved and validated OplmConfig. If a YAML file was used,
596	        ``cfg.train.config_path`` is populated with its absolute path. ``--name``
597	        sets ``cfg.train.wandb_run_name`` unless that field was explicitly set in
598	        the YAML or via a CLI override (an explicit value always wins); when both
599	        are unset it stays ``None`` (W&B assigns a random name). ``--name`` also
600	        seeds ``cfg.train.output_dir`` to ``./<name>`` unless ``train.output_dir``
601	        was explicitly set in the YAML or via a CLI override.
602	    """
603	    base: DictConfig = OmegaConf.structured(OplmConfig)
604	
605	    # Disable struct mode to allow dynamic keys under data.train
606	    # (data.train can be a string path or a nested dict of datasets).
607	    OmegaConf.set_struct(base, False)
608	
609	    # Authoritative YAML defaults layer (model → train → data). These are the
610	    # human-editable home for defaults and override the dataclass fallbacks.
611	    for package, filename in _BASE_CONFIG_LAYERS:
612	        base = cast("DictConfig", OmegaConf.merge(base, _load_packaged_yaml(package, filename)))
613	
614	    # Extract --config, --preset, and --name flags
615	    config_path: str | None = None
616	    preset: str | None = None
617	    run_name: str | None = None
618	    remaining: list[str] = []
619	    i = 0
620	    while i < len(argv):
621	        if argv[i] == "--config" and i + 1 < len(argv):
622	            config_path = str(Path(argv[i + 1]).expanduser().resolve())
623	            i += 2
624	        elif argv[i] == "--preset" and i + 1 < len(argv):
625	            preset = argv[i + 1]
626	            i += 2
627	        elif argv[i] == "--name" and i + 1 < len(argv):
628	            run_name = argv[i + 1]
629	            i += 2
630	        else:
631	            remaining.append(argv[i])
632	            i += 1
633	
634	    # Collect user overrides (preset → --config → CLI dotlist), applied on top
635	    # of the authoritative base layer.
636	    overrides: list[DictConfig] = []
637	    if preset is not None:
638	        overrides.append(get_preset_config(preset))
639	    if config_path is not None:
640	        overrides.append(cast("DictConfig", OmegaConf.load(config_path)))
641	    if remaining:
642	        overrides.append(OmegaConf.from_dotlist(remaining))
643	
644	    override_dicts = [OmegaConf.to_container(ov, resolve=True) for ov in overrides]
645	    _reject_removed_sequence_length_alias(override_dicts)
646	
647	    # Whether the user explicitly set the W&B run name (YAML or CLI override).
648	    # An explicit value — even ``null`` — wins over the ``--name`` flag below.
649	    user_set_run_name = any(
650	        _lookup_nested_mapping_value(ov, ("train", "wandb_run_name")) is not _NESTED_VALUE_MISSING
651	        for ov in override_dicts
652	    )
653	
654	    # Whether the user explicitly set the output directory (YAML or CLI override).
655	    # An explicit value wins over the ``--name``-derived default below.
656	    user_set_output_dir = any(
657	        _lookup_nested_mapping_value(ov, ("train", "output_dir")) is not _NESTED_VALUE_MISSING
658	        for ov in override_dicts
659	    )
660	
661	    # Merge all overrides into base
662	    for ov in overrides:
663	        base = cast("DictConfig", OmegaConf.merge(base, ov))
664	
665	    # Build train/data dataclasses (triggers their __post_init__ validation);
666	    # `model` is an Any field so it round-trips as a plain dict here.
667	    cfg: OplmConfig = OmegaConf.to_object(base)  # ty: ignore[invalid-assignment]  # OmegaConf union
668	
669	    # Instantiate the HF model config from the merged `model` subtree. HF owns
670	    # derivation (head_dim, intermediate_size, rope_dim/nope_dim) and validation.
671	    # Derived fields are omitted unless set, resolving to None → derived inside
672	    # OplmModelConfig.__init__. Unknown / mistyped `model.*` keys are rejected
673	    # here (run-config path) rather than silently absorbed into
674	    # PretrainedConfig **kwargs; from_pretrained() stays permissive for
675	    # checkpoint compatibility.
676	    from oplm.model import OplmConfig as OplmModelConfig
677	
678	    model_dict = cast("dict[str, Any]", OmegaConf.to_container(base.model, resolve=True) or {})
679	    _reject_unknown_model_keys(model_dict, OplmModelConfig)
680	    cfg.model = OplmModelConfig(**model_dict)
681	
682	    # Cross-config divisibility check: pad_to_multiple_of must evenly divide
683	    # max_position_embeddings so padded lengths can never overflow position IDs.
684	    # This is the only place both cfg.data and the resolved cfg.model are available.
685	    if cfg.data.pad_to_multiple_of is not None:

# These are OPLM's opinionated *production* defaults: μP + Muon, with `lr` as the
# μP base LR (see docs/MUP.md). They intentionally differ from the conservative
# oplm.config.TrainConfig dataclass fallbacks (adamw / lr 1e-4 / match_rms_adamw),

# Every user-settable TrainConfig option appears here set to its default; the one

train:
  # Duration
  max_steps: 50_000
  max_epochs: null

  # Batch
  batch_size: 32
  gradient_accumulation_steps: 1

  # Optimizer — μP + Muon is the default recipe (disable via configs/train/vanilla_esm-c.yaml).
  optimizer: muon             # adamw | muon
  # μP base learning rate. With μP on (the default; model.mup_enable), this value
  # transfers across model width automatically — do NOT retune it per preset/size.
  # Tuned at mup_base_width=768 (Muon, adjust_lr_fn=original) via the phased sweep
  # in docs/LR_SWEEP.md; 800M confirm winner, Aug 2026. Only retune if you DISABLE
  # μP (e.g. via configs/train/vanilla_esm-c.yaml), where it is no longer
  # width-correct.
  lr: 0.0035
  min_lr: 0.0
  weight_decay: 0.01
  adam_beta1: 0.9
  adam_beta2: 0.98
  adam_eps: 1.0e-8
  # μP + Muon REQUIRES "original" (aspect-ratio-only, ~constant across width so the
  # base LR transfers). "match_rms_adamw" scales like √width and does NOT transfer;
  # build_optimizers raises if it is left on with μP + Muon.
  muon_adjust_lr_fn: original          # match_rms_adamw | original
  muon_momentum: 0.95
  muon_nesterov: true
  muon_ns_steps: 5
  # Empirical repeated-block LR correction for the production scaling ray:
  # hidden LR × (reference_layers / L) ** exponent. 0.5 is derived from the
  # α=1/√L residual scaling and verified on the sweep's fixed-width depth ray;
  # it is exactly 1.0 at the 24-layer (170M anchor) reference depth.
  mup_depth_lr_exponent: 0.5
  mup_depth_reference_layers: 24
  max_grad_norm: 1.0

  # Scheduler
  scheduler: warmup_linear    # warmup_linear | warmup_cosine | wsd_linear | wsd_cosine
  warmup_steps: 5_000
  stable_steps: 0             # WSD plateau length (WSD schedules only)

  log_every: 10
  # Default eval cadence for datasets that omit `every`: {steps: N} | {tokens: N}.
  # Left null so an override replaces it cleanly (a non-null dict would deep-merge
  # and collide on the unit key); null resolves to {steps: 10_000} in the Evaluator.
  eval_every: null
  wandb_project: oplm
  wandb_run_name: null
  wandb_enabled: true

  # Checkpointing
  save_every: 10_000
  save_total_limit: 3
  save_final: true            # write a final checkpoint on completion (skips if last step already saved)
  # Also checkpoint every N wall-clock minutes, in addition to (not instead of)
  # the save_every step cadence; null disables the timer, > 0 if set.
  save_every_minutes: null
  # Retain (exempt from save_total_limit rotation) every checkpoint whose step is
  # a multiple of N; null disables the exemption, > 0 if set.
  keep_every_n_steps: null
  # Retain a checkpoint at least every N wall-clock hours after the previous
  # permanent one; null disables the exemption, > 0 if set.
  keep_every_n_hours: null
  resume_from: null           # path to a checkpoint to resume from
  # Automatically resume from the newest committed checkpoint under output_dir at
  # trainer start, without an explicit resume_from (long Slurm runs set this true).
  auto_resume: false
  # On resume, also restore the data-loader position (sampler/shard offsets) so
  # training continues from the same data point instead of restarting the stream.
  resume_data_position: true
  # Optional remote URI (e.g. s3://bucket/prefix) that committed checkpoints are
  # additionally synced to; null disables remote sync. s3:// needs the `s3` extra.
  remote_checkpoint_uri: null

  # Infrastructure
  seed: 42
  output_dir: outputs
  # ddp  — one full model replica per rank (default).
  # hsdp — FSDP2 over a 2-D mesh (shard within a node, replicate across nodes);
  #        required before ~24B, needs world size > 1, and is currently
  #        incompatible with configured data.eval (see docs/TRAIN.md).
  parallelism: ddp            # ddp | hsdp
  # Process-group timeout (minutes); longer tolerates slow checkpoint writes or
  # requeue delays without a collective abort. Must be > 0.
  dist_timeout_minutes: 15
  mixed_precision: bf16       # bf16 | fp16 | no
  compile: false
  compile_mode: default       # default | reduce-overhead | max-autotune
  compile_dynamic: true   # true | false | null(auto) — torch.compile dynamic flag
  throughput_warmup_steps: 50
  peak_tflops: null   # set device peak (TFLOPs) to log MFU

  # entropy under diag/*) every stability_probe_every log emissions.
  stability_diagnostics: false
  stability_probe_every: 25   # probe cadence in log emissions; 0 logs only the grad norm
